title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context (abstract page)
note: Fetched. v1 submitted 21 Sep 2026, CC BY 4.0. Announces open-weight t0-alpha (102M) and t0-beta (256M) that take target history, past and known-future covariates without retraining. Headline: GIFT-Eval CRPS 0.4941 and 0.4738, fev-bench skill 42.2 and 46.7, a 6.3-point lift from known-future covariates over 30 tasks.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context (full text)
note: Fetched. Covariate ablation on fev-bench, same t0-alpha checkpoint with and without covariates: skill 36.7 to 43.0 on the 30 known-future tasks (+6.3, 95% bootstrap interval +2.2 to +10.9, 19 of 30 improve) and 32.9 to 35.6 on 12 past-only tasks (+2.7, +1.0 to +4.2). Eleven known-future tasks get worse; the worst is 15% on a 15-minute electricity series with weather covariates.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context (full text)
note: Fetched. Public benchmarks. GIFT-Eval (97 configurations, no covariates used): alpha CRPS 0.4941, MASE 0.7240, 11th of 17 zero-shot models; beta CRPS 0.4738, MASE 0.6865, third. fev-bench skill: alpha 42.2 under the benchmark's imputation rule, beta 46.7. TIME CRPS: beta 0.5551. Eight fev-bench tasks are declared as in alpha's pretraining data, including GEFCom load.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context (full text)
note: Fetched. Victoria (Australia) hourly demand case, following a skforecast guide: 24 h ahead, realized temperature and a holiday flag as known-future inputs, 62 one-day windows, Oct 31 to Dec 31 2024 (rerun on 2024 because 2014 is in the pretraining corpus). MAE in MW at 8192 h context: Chronos-2 324.24, t0-beta 334.92, t0-alpha 372.51, 24 h seasonal naive 614.57. At 512 h: 348.87, 368.89, 379.58.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context (full text)
note: Fetched. ERCOT section, written by Macrocosm as an outside evaluation: hourly real-time prices in four load zones, Jan 2024 to May 2026, day-ahead issue at 09:00, 21 covariates (load, renewables, outages, weather). The abstract says both models cut the MAE of a repeat-last-day price baseline by 38%. Price, not load; the baseline gets no covariates.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context (full text)
note: Fetched. Training and limits: pretraining mixes public corpora (including the GIFT-Eval pretraining set) with synthetic series built to contain covariate effects; the text says every real series in the corpus ends before 2022. Horizons up to 1024 steps decode in one pass. No pre-registration is mentioned. The report covers alpha and beta only, not gamma.

title: theforecastingcompany/t0-gamma model card
note: Fetched. Third t0 release, about 256M parameters, Apache-2.0, needs tfc-t0 0.6.1 or later, takes future_covariates over context plus horizon, 21 native quantiles, 1024 steps in one pass. Card table, gamma vs beta: GIFT-Eval CRPS 0.4503 vs 0.4738, MASE 0.6580 vs 0.6865; fev-bench skill 49.40 vs 46.65; TIME CRPS 0.5340 vs 0.5551, MASE 0.6370 vs 0.6647.

title: Time-Series LLMs, Explained with t0-alpha (Sean Moran)
note: Fetched. An outside author reruns t0-alpha on GIFT-Eval on a rented GPU and gets CRPS 0.4941 and MASE 0.7240, matching the published figures to four decimals; other rows in the comparison are official numbers, not reruns. No covariates and no load-specific test. Notes tuned MSTL narrows the gap on high-frequency tasks.
